title: [Interactive Brokers] Modify during Gateway connectivity loss can duplicate the order at IB (new permId, original stays live); adapter tracks one incarnation and cancel leaves an orphaned working order
body:
## Bug report

**Adapter:** Interactive Brokers
**Version:** `1.231.0a20260709` (develop nightly), Python 3.13, Linux (Docker), gnzsnz `ib-gateway` (paper)

### Summary

An order modified with a normal in-place `placeOrder` (same IB `orderId`) **while the TWS↔IBKR connectivity was degraded/lost** was resolved by IB as a **new working order with a new `permId`, while the original `permId` stayed live** — two real broker orders from one modify. The adapter cannot represent "one client order → two broker incarnations", so:

1. On reconnect, IB's open-order snapshots replayed **both** incarnations; `_on_open_order` overwrites the cached `venue_order_id` last-writer-wins (`venue_order_id_modified=True`), and the **stale original** incarnation arrived last, leaving the engine tracking the wrong order.
2. A later `cancel_order` resolved and cancelled only that one incarnation. IB confirmed `OrderCanceled` — but the *modified* incarnation kept working at the broker, invisible to the engine.
3. Six hours later the surviving incarnation **filled** (4 contracts, a protective stop → an unintended position flip). The fill report carried the surviving `permId`, so `Order.apply` raised `ValueError('self.venue_order_id' ... was not equal to 'event.venue_order_id' ...)` against the CANCELED order, and the engine fell back to inferred-fill NET reconciliation (which healed positions correctly — but the harm was the orphaned order executing at all).

### Timeline (UTC, 2026-07-24, paper account, MESU6.CME)

```
06:10:03  submit STOP_MARKET BUY 4 @ 7463.75 GTC  -> OrderAccepted venue_order_id=PERM-253949451 (IB orderId=187)
06:14:08  ERROR InteractiveBrokersClient: Not connected (code 504)
06:14:13  ERROR Client failed to initialize; connection timeout
06:15:08  ModifyOrder trigger 7463.75 -> 7443.75; adapter logs exactly ONE
          "Placing 136287796088976: 187,0,0: STP BUY 4@ GTC"  (in-place, same orderId=187)
06:15:14+ modify never confirms; engine in-flight check queries every ~2s
06:30:05  ERROR Connectivity between IBKR and TWS has been lost (code 1100); watchdog reconnect
06:30:06  OrderUpdated venue_order_id=PERM-253949452 trigger=7443.75 + OrderAccepted (the modified incarnation, NEW permId)
06:30:10  OrderUpdated venue_order_id=PERM-253949451 trigger=7463.75  (the ORIGINAL, still working; cache clobbered back to 451)
07:10:02  CancelOrder (resolves 451) -> OrderCanceled confirmed.  PERM-253949452 remains working at IB.
13:30:00  IB fills PERM-253949452 BUY 4 @ 7444.00
13:30:23  position check: cached_qty=-2 venue_qty=2 -> missing-fill query ->
          ERROR ExecEngine: Error on applying OrderFilled(... venue_order_id=PERM-253949452 ...)
          ValueError('self.venue_order_id' ... PERM-253949451 was not equal to ... PERM-253949452)
          -> inferred NET reconciliation heals positions
```

### Verification that a *clean* modify is fine

Reproduced live against the same Gateway/account (second API client id, unfillable far-from-market LIMIT, qty 1): place → in-place modify (same `orderId`) → **`permId` unchanged, exactly one working order** → cancel → clean. So the duplication is specifically an IB-side artifact of a modify issued into/around a connectivity loss; the adapter's modify path itself places once, in place. (The duplication itself was not re-induced — it requires forcing a Gateway reconnect on a live-traded account.)

### Where the adapter makes it worse (source refs, `adapters/interactive_brokers/execution.py` @ 1.231.0a20260709)

- `_on_open_order` (~L1789 → L1842–L1848): unconditionally rewrites the cached `venue_order_id` to whatever the latest open-order snapshot reports. When IB replays two incarnations of the same `orderRef`, last-writer-wins silently selects one — in our case the stale, about-to-be-cancelled one. There is no detection of "this client order already has a *different* live venue id".
- `_cancel_order` (~L1524): resolves a single IB `orderId` (via `_resolve_ib_order_id`, ~L1602) and cancels a single order — a duplicate incarnation it doesn't know about survives.
- The continuous open-order check (`open_check_interval_secs`) *does* see the survivor every cycle, but because the report maps back (via `orderRef`) to the CANCELED client order with a different `venue_order_id`, applying it hits the same mismatch wall — so it can only log the error repeatedly, never heal or cancel the orphan.

### Suggested directions

1. After a modify/cancel (or on reconnect), reconcile the **instrument-level open-order set**: if one `client_order_id`/`orderRef` maps to more than one live `permId`, surface it (event or at minimum a WARN with both ids) instead of silently clobbering `venue_order_id`.
2. In `_on_open_order`, don't overwrite a cached `venue_order_id` with a *different* id while the order is in an open state without flagging the conflict.
3. Optionally: a post-cancel verification (order-status query) so `OrderCanceled` on one incarnation isn't treated as "nothing else with this orderRef is working".

Happy to provide the full node logs for the incident window.
